messages:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a 3h profiling sweep across c4 pools. saw a sharp latency tail when decode-rate falls into the 8-12 tk/s bucket and prompt lengths in 512-768. suspect kernel selection flip + KV cache churn. attaching short dump below. :eyes:

sara: can you paste the profiler snippet? curious if it's a kernel swap (fp16->int8) or memory thrash from KV reads.

alex: here — rough excerpt from the pprof + kernel logs:
```
bucket: decode_rate=9 tk/s, len=600
selected_kernel: matmul_q8_opt_v2
observed_kernel: matmul_fp16_fallback
avg_latency: 142ms (p50 65ms, p95 520ms)
kv_hits: 68%, kv_misses: 32%, kv_read_bytes/s: 42MB
concurrent_batches: 3 -> queue waited 46ms before admission
```

mike: that kernel mismatch is the smoking gun. why did runtime flip to fp16_fallback? recent kernel selector change to prefer stability for mixed-length sequences?

alex: selector change from yesterday: prefer kernels with lower p95 across full profile, but we didn't gate on decode-rate buckets. when runtime sees sparse KV hits + longer loops, it picked safer kernel. regress in p95.

jen: could also be token budget interaction — if token_budget per-worker is low we end up with smaller microbatches and the selector prefers FP16 (safer) and gives up on q8 path because throughput estimate is noisy. what are current token_budget targets?

alex: defaults: token_budget_target=120 per GPU, admission_policy=latency_pref. but for these traffic patterns we need a different target. lowered budgets for short bursts -> more kernel switches.

sara: proposal: add a probe that ties kernel selection decision to a 2-d classification: (prompt_length_bucket, decode_rate_bucket). simplest: override kernel score by +X when (len in 512-1024, decode_rate 6-14) to favor q8 kernel. also increase token_budget_target -> 200 for that cohort.

mike: +1. also we should tweak queue routing: keep slices with predicted decode_rate>6 in the same admission pool to avoid cross-pollination causing kv thrash. basically isolate medium-rate, mid-length cohort.

alex: i sketched a config change. dropped as a canary YAML for the allocator/prober:
```yaml
cohorts:
  - name: midlen_medrate
    prompt_len: [512,1024]
    decode_rate: [6,14]
    token_budget_target: 200
    kernel_bias: {matmul_q8_opt_v2: +0.12}
    admission_pool: medium_rate_isolated
```

jen: love it. can we also add a tiny metric emitted from runtime when kernel_bias applied (bool) so perf dashboards can show correlation?

alex: yes — added metric flag kernel_bias_applied{cohort="midlen_medrate"}. will emit counts and latency histogram.

ci-bot: perf-check started for branch refs/heads/heuristic/midlen-cohort-canary — running 2h smoke (GPU: c4-small x4).

mike: after canary, we should run a stress with artificially induced KV miss rate to ensure no regression in throughput for heavy-embedding workloads. also add a rollback window of 30m if p95 increases by >15%.

alex: agreed. scheduling canary now. plan: 2h canary -> 4h extended if p95 stable -> roll to 10% traffic. I'll post results. :thumbsup:

sara: if this goes well, next step is an automated classifier that updates cohorts from online stats (every 6h) — not manual YAML. but for now canary is good.

jen: small nits: expose token_budget_target as per-GPU AND per-admission-pool so we can fine tune.

alex: noted. thanks all — will dump canary logs here when ci-bot finishes.

ci-bot: perf-check completed: canary p95 down 18% for midlen_medrate cohort, overall p95 stable, kv_miss rate unchanged. marking as success. :white_check_mark:

mike: awesome. open PR to bake this into allocator and add dashboard panels for kernel_bias_applied.

alex: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/infra/heuristics/+/432 — includes config, metric emit, and canary notes.

sara: great work. follow-up: schedule retro next week to generalize to other kernels and add automated cohort discovery. :party_parrot:
